info.name: MongoDB Atlas Administration Access Tracking X.509 Authentication API
Return All X.509 Certificates Assigned to One Database User

params.name: envelope
params.description: Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.

params.name: groupId
params.description:
Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.

**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.

params.name: includeCount
params.description: Flag that indicates whether the response returns the total number of items (`totalCount`) in the response.

params.name: itemsPerPage
params.description: Number of items that the response returns per page.

params.name: pageNum
params.description: Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.

params.name: pretty
params.description: Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.

params.name: username
params.description: Human-readable label that represents the MongoDB database user account whose certificates you want to return.

items.docs: Returns all unexpired X.509 certificates for the specified MongoDB user. This MongoDB user belongs to one project. Atlas manages these certificates and the MongoDB user. To use this resource, the requesting Service Account or API Key must have the Project Read Only role.

items.docs:
Generates one X.509 certificate for the specified MongoDB user. Atlas manages the certificate and MongoDB user that belong to one project. To use this resource, the requesting Service Account or API Key must have the Project Owner role.

To get MongoDB Cloud to generate a managed certificate for a database user, set `"x509Type" : "MANAGED"` on the desired MongoDB Database User.

Clears the customer-managed X.509 settings on a project, including the uploaded Certificate Authority, which disables self-managed X.509.

 Updating this configuration triggers a rolling restart of the database. You must have the Project Owner role to use this endpoint.
